dedupe_keys.name: nsf platforms for advanced wireless research pawr powder cosmos aerpaw and ara city scale and rural wireless testbeds

description: The Platforms for Advanced Wireless Research (PAWR) programme runs four city-scale and rural wireless testbeds, all listed as generally available, plus the Colosseum emulator as a facility. Coverage: sites in the United States. POWDER, in Salt Lake City, supports software-defined experiments on 5G and beyond, massive MIMO, O-RAN, spectrum sharing and CBRS, with a wired bench, attenuator matrix, indoor lab, a campus-wide outdoor deployment and radios on campus shuttles. COSMOS is a city-scale testbed in West Harlem, New York, of software-defined radio nodes with fibre front-haul and back-haul and edge cloud computing, focused on high bandwidth and low latency. AERPAW, led by NC State, studies 5G with autonomous drones. ARA, in rural Iowa, is at-scale infrastructure for rural wireless, with agriculture applications and satellite links. Format and access: remote experiments through each platform's portal after requesting an account, under acceptable use policies; some platforms publish measurement data. Licence: not applicable to the testbeds; data terms vary by platform and were not read. Caveats: access is aimed at researchers; terms, costs and eligibility were not read. Simulation uses: over-the-air experiments and digital twins of 5G, O-RAN and spectrum sharing for capacity planning and resilience of wireless networks. Related records: Colosseum (platform-colosseum-open-ran-digital-twin) is the programme's emulator, and FABRIC (platform-fabric-research-network-testbed) is a related NSF research infrastructure.
